---
title: "Research"
---

My research lies at the intersection of **stochastic control, optimization, applied probability, and decision-making under uncertainty**. I am particularly interested in mathematical models in which decisions must be made under incomplete information, model ambiguity, or randomly evolving environments.

My current research can be broadly organized into three interconnected areas.

## Stochastic Control and Markov Jump Systems

A significant part of my research concerns the analysis and control of dynamical systems subject to random regime changes, with particular emphasis on **Markov jump linear systems** and problems in which the underlying operating mode is only partially observed.

My work in this area includes robust control, filtering, stability analysis, and detector-based approaches for systems with incomplete mode information. I am particularly interested in how partial information and stochastic switching affect the design of controllers and estimators, and in developing mathematically tractable methods that can be implemented computationally.

## Distributionally Robust Optimization and Decision-Making under Uncertainty

More recently, my research has focused on **decision-making under model ambiguity**, particularly in settings where the probability distributions governing the system are not known exactly.

I am interested in distributionally robust formulations in which uncertainty is represented through ambiguity sets around nominal probabilistic models. Current topics include KL-divergence ambiguity sets, optimization over probability distributions, robust policy design, and free-energy-based formulations of decision-making.

A central objective of this research is to develop methods that are both mathematically rigorous and computationally implementable, particularly for problems involving nested optimization and worst-case probabilistic models.

### Selected related work

* **Free-Energy Minimizing Policies Under Generative Model Ambiguity**
  A. Shafiei, C. C. Graciani Rodrigues, and G. Russo
  *European Control Conference (ECC)*, 2026.
  [arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.08222)

## Stochastic Games and Mathematical Finance

Another strand of my research concerns **strategic decision-making under uncertainty**, particularly through stochastic games and applications to mathematical finance.

I am interested in models in which multiple decision-makers interact dynamically while facing stochastic economic or environmental conditions. These problems naturally combine stochastic control, game theory, optimal stopping, and free-boundary methods.

Recent work in this direction studies strategic sustainable investment decisions and the interaction between firms and investors when investment opportunities and economic conditions evolve randomly.

### Selected related work

* **A Model of Strategic Sustainable Investment**
  T. De Angelis, C. C. Graciani Rodrigues, and P. Tankov
